name: contextgem-enconvo
title: ContextGem
description: Structured document and text extraction with the ContextGem framework, running on your Enconvo LLM providers through a local bridge — no API keys to manage. Route closed questions to Jev on Enconvo Cloud for calibrated probabilities. Aspects and typed concepts (string, boolean, numerical, date, rating, JSON, label) come back with justifications, source references and usage stats; save reusable pipelines; extract from files with the optional docling extra.
short_description: Structured extraction on your Enconvo LLMs, with optional Jev decisions
author: Iteractive Development

commands.name: extract
commands.title: ContextGem Extract
commands.description: Extract structured data from text, a pasted document or an attached file. Input: JSON {"text"|"file_path", "aspects":[{"name","description"}], "concepts":[{"type","name","description"}], "engine":"llm"|"decision_model"|"auto", "pipeline":"<saved name>"}. Attached files are used as the document (needs the docling extra).

preferences.name: llm
preferences.title: LLM Model
preferences.description: The Enconvo LLM provider and model that run the extraction, using the key you already manage under Settings › Credentials. Defaults to your default LLM.

commands.name: doctor
commands.title: ContextGem Doctor
commands.description: Check the Python environment, the ContextGem install, the optional docling extra, which Enconvo LLM provider would run through the chat bridge, and whether Jev answers closed questions — and print what to fix when something is off. Run with the input setup to create or repair the environment in one shot.

preferences.name: llm
preferences.title: LLM Model
preferences.description: The Enconvo LLM provider and model that run the extraction, using the key you already manage under Settings › Credentials. Defaults to your default LLM.

preferences.name: decision_engine
preferences.title: Decision Engine
preferences.description: On by default: route closed questions (booleans, labels, ratings) to Jev through Enconvo Cloud for calibrated probabilities, billed as points. Uses the app's own sign-in; no key to manage. If Jev is unavailable, auto runs fall back to the LLM.

preferences.name: python_bin
preferences.title: Python Binary
preferences.description: Python used to build the plugin's private environment. Empty auto-detects a Python 3.11-3.14; python3, python3.12 or an absolute path also work. Only read when the environment is created.

preferences.name: install_docling
preferences.title: Install Docling (file support)
preferences.description: Also install contextgem[docling] during setup so PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX and HTML files can be extracted. Large download (PyTorch); without it the plugin extracts from text only.

preferences.name: timeout_seconds
preferences.title: Extraction Timeout (seconds)
preferences.description: How long one extraction may run before it is stopped (30-3600). Large documents and many aspects take longer.

positive.prompt: On a fresh install, POST {} to /api/contextgem-enconvo/setup.
positive.expected_behavior: A venv is created under ~/.config/enconvo/.support/contextgem-enconvo (uv when present), contextgem installs and imports, and status reports ready true.

positive.description: Extraction runs through the chat bridge on any Enconvo provider.
positive.prompt: With any Enconvo LLM provider selected, POST a short invoice text with a string concept (add_justifications true, add_references true) to /api/contextgem-enconvo/extract.
positive.expected_behavior: Items come back with value, justification and reference paragraphs; the request carries no API key, and stats.llm.usage reports tokens from the provider.

positive.description: Jev answers closed questions through the decision bridge.
positive.prompt: With the Decision Engine set to Jev and engine auto, POST a contract clause with a boolean concept.
positive.expected_behavior: The closed question is relayed to Enconvo Cloud with the app session token; items carry calibrated probabilities, and no TypeSafe key exists anywhere in the plugin.

positive.prompt: POST pipeline_save {name: invoices, concepts: [...]}, then extract with {pipeline: invoices, text}, then pipeline_delete.
positive.expected_behavior: The saved spec applies when the request omits aspects/concepts, lists in pipeline_list, and deletes cleanly.

Checks for Python 3.11-3.14, the venv, contextgem with version, docling, the bundled runner, the Enconvo LLM provider that would run via the chat bridge, and the Decision Engine, ending with an Overall line.

positive.description: Attached files convert with docling when the extra is installed.
positive.prompt: With Install Docling enabled and setup re-run, attach a PDF and give aspects to extract.
positive.expected_behavior: The file converts through docling and extraction returns items; without the extra the error names DOCLING_MISSING and the preference to enable.

negative.description: No document is rejected before any model runs.
negative.prompt: POST /extract with only a concept and no text or file_path.
negative.expected_behavior: HTTP 400 BAD_INPUT "provide text or file_path"; nothing is billed.

negative.description: Bad specs are named, not discovered by the model.
negative.prompt: POST /extract with dry_run true and a rating concept without rating_scale.
negative.expected_behavior: HTTP 400 BAD_SPEC naming the concept and the missing field.

negative.description: The decision engine is demanded, not silently ignored.
negative.prompt: With Decision Engine off, POST /extract with engine decision_model and a boolean concept.
negative.expected_behavior: HTTP 400 BAD_SPEC telling the user to set the Decision Engine preference to Jev; no LLM call happens.

negative.description: An unknown provider is refused, never silently substituted.
negative.prompt: POST /extract with llm_provider set to a name that is not configured.
negative.expected_behavior: HTTP 409 LLM_UNAVAILABLE naming the provider and where to fix it.

negative.description: Jev without a Cloud session fails with the fix.
negative.prompt: With Decision Engine set to Jev and Enconvo Cloud signed out, run a boolean extraction.
negative.expected_behavior: A typed error naming the Enconvo Cloud sign-in; never a hang and never a leaked bridge token.

negative.prompt: Force a failure (bad endpoint via llm_options) and read the whole error response.
negative.expected_behavior: Bridge tokens and any api_key are absent from the response body and from what the runner prints.

negative.description: Evidence flags on Jev-extracted targets are rejected up front.
negative.prompt: With Decision Engine set to Jev, POST an auto-engine extraction with a boolean concept carrying add_justifications true and dry_run true.
negative.expected_behavior: HTTP 400 BAD_SPEC naming the concept and the two fixes (drop the flags or set model_role extractor); no decision is billed.
